groups.text: A refund ledger has a race.
A test starts two threads, each makes one refund, and checks the total.
It passes, every time.
Starting a thread takes a while, and one refund is over in a moment.
They never overlap, so the race never happens.
How would you make them collide?
Hold every thread at a start latch, then release them all at once.
Use more threads than cores, and many operations each, so they overlap for a long time.
Run many rounds with fresh state.
Each round is one sample of the interleavings.
After join, check an invariant.
Eight threads try two thousand one-cent refunds each, against one zero zero zero zero cents.
A correct ledger approves exactly one zero zero zero zero.
The racy one approves one six zero zero zero.
On the lesson's racy counter, the naive test failed at most six of twenty runs.
The stress test failed all twenty.
Next, waiting. This test submits a payment, sleeps fifty milliseconds, then checks that it settled.
On a busy CI machine, the work runs longer.
The check comes too soon, and the test fails for no reason.
In the lesson's runs, it failed about a quarter of the time.
Instead, wait for the event.
A latch counts down when the payment settles, and the test awaits it, with a deadline of ten seconds.
Fast when the work is fast, patient when the machine is slow.
It failed zero times.
In Java and Kotlin, it is the same four lines.
Some races need millions of tries.
jcstress, the OpenJDK harness, does that.
Two actors increment one counter, and record what they read.
It runs this millions of times, and counts each outcome.
one, two and two, one are acceptable.
one, one means both read zero, so an increment was lost.
It is labeled interesting: the race you are looking for.
Label an outcome forbidden, and one sighting fails the test.
The rule. Make threads collide on purpose, wait for events instead of time, and read a pass as: not found this time.
Check yourself. A test starts two threads, each makes one refund, and it has never failed.
Is the ledger safe?
You can't tell.
The refunds probably never overlapped.
A pass only means this run found nothing.
